newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open flat to $5 higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open flat to $5 higher.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open unchanged to $5 higher Monday, in line with gains in London overnight, traders said.

LIFFE cocoa futures were firmer in dull dealings early Monday, helped by a weak sterling. At the midday break, July cocoa was up seven stg at 1,018 stg a tonne, with September three stg higher at 1,030 stg.

Friday, New York cocoa futures ended broadly high and near the top of the day's range, but trading was exceedingly thin. July futures finished up $18 at $1,440 a tonne after trading from $1,441 to $1,420. Spot May, which goes off the boards next week, rose the same to $1,430, while the remaining months ended between $14 and $16 higher.
Technically, traders said July would need to breach resistance at $1,450 to encourage enthusiastic buying, while support was seen toward Friday's low of $1,420.

CFTC's Commitments fo Traders report for the two weeks ended May 6 showed noncommercial long positions fell by 4,835 lots, to 10,903 lots, while noncommerial short positions rose by 2,682 lots to 5,170 lots.
Commercial long positions in the two weeks rose by 3,738 lots, to 68,013 lots, and commerial short positions fell by 4,162 lots to 80,326 lots.
Non-reportable long positions rose by 760 lots, to 14,250 lots, while nonreportable short positions rose by 1,143 lots to 7,670 lots.

Broker GNI said in its daily comment the CFTC report showing a sharp reduction in fund longs over the past two weeks and an increase in commercial longs was constructive for cocoa. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk 212 859 1640))
